correctness.rationale: The specified polynomial g divides x^23+1 and its twelve degree-separated message shifts form an injective enumeration of all 4096 binary Golay words. The zero-run identity computes cyclic b-read weights exactly and all 81 run classes yield each of 23 complete spectra. A separately implemented direct-window polynomial-division verifier checked every coefficient, all 4096 words, exact minima/multiplicities, the single minimizer orbit for b=3..11, and the classical Hamming spectrum. Stabilization for b>=12 follows additionally from the constant term of g forcing all message coefficients to vanish if 12 consecutive zeros occur. Finite full exhaustion is sufficient for this exact length-23 theorem, not a claim about other lengths.

originality.rationale: The known distance values at widths 1 through 11 are fully covered by Guan et al. (2025), the b>=12 stabilization is covered by Shi–Özbudak–Solé (2021), the general pair bound is covered by Yaakobi–Bruck–Siegel (2016), and the elementary run identity is prior art (also used for ternary Golay in 2026). These facts are expressly not claimed novel. The new claim is the binary Golay code’s complete nontrivial width-2-through-11 coefficient multiplicities, 81-class joint zero-run census, and 23-word common minimizing orbit for widths 3 through 11, which the inspected papers do not give. Direct source implication checks plus targeted exact-table and alias searches did not identify coverage of those data. Residual risk remains from unindexed historical tables.
residual_risks: The indexed literature and abstract checks do not exclude an unindexed historical Golay zero-run table or full b-symbol spectrum; definitive priority is not certified.
The Zhu–Shi–Özbudak adjacent irreducible-code paper was not examined in its entirety; the stated irreducibility premise is an inapplicable but not complete full-text exclusion.
Independent scientific review beyond the author-side finite certificate and its separately implemented checker has not been performed.
Original HAL source of the 2021 general stability paper was access-restricted; its scope was inspected through author-posted full text and verified abstracts, but not a complete direct HAL PDF.

value.rationale: The natural full b-symbol spectrum is needed for precise error-weight multiplicities of a canonical cyclic perfect code. Previously published Golay results give only the 11-entry minimum-distance hierarchy, and a general stability theorem covers trivial large widths; neither resolves all coefficient multiplicities at the genuinely variable widths 2 through 11. This exact 81-class zero-run and 23-by-24 coefficient classification, including the common 23-word minimizing orbit over nine widths, provides substantial reproducible structural information beyond all covered old distance results, rather than rebranding a known minimum or an arbitrary finite calculation.
